content: I hope you received enough feedback from the community to improve your contribution. Once you have made the necessary updates, publish your contribution!
Please let me know when you're done updating the text and the cases (as per @yhuberla 's comments), and I'll review the contribution then. Thank you!

This will be fun to solve :)

For now though it's a bit hard for me to grasp, could you add some smaller test cases (with only a couple lines) to introduce the concepts bit by bit ? As for now, from the very first test case, we use subleq, labels, offsets, memory addresses, ins and outs (==everything).

I also advocate for a step by step explanation on what really happens (order of execution and content of registers) with a small test case, similar to what puzzles https://www.codingame.com/training/hard/simple-cpu-emulation-1 and https://www.codingame.com/training/medium/micro-assembly have done.

Cheers.
I need to refine the text, and enhance both tests and validators. I look forward to your feedback. Thank you.

Sure, that sounds like great advice. I'll work on it. Thank you.
PS. there are no registers, only memory :-)
I fix the text with @yhuberla 's comments. Thanks!

Goal
* Please change "a full 256 bytes of memory" to "a full memory of 256 bytes".

* Suggest to add a heading "<<Memory and number handling>>" near the beginning.

* "(in the source code there are no spaces between the sign − and the number)": Please change this to a new sentence and remove the brackets. Please also change "the number" to "the digits of a negative number".

* Please format the following as {{constants}}:
  • - (negative sign)
  • subleq and the two commas
  • @, :, +, +1
  • .data
  • @IN
  • @OUT

* Please format the following as [[variables]]:
  • A, B, C
  • label
  • X

* Suggest to use another letter to replace "x" in "address x" to avoid confusion with "X" in ".data X".

* Assembler Instructions
  • Please mention that instructions may contain blank lines and trailing spaces.

  • Please explain how addresses are determined. In the example, you have explained how to determine the addresses at @datazone and @pos, but please explain the GENERAL LOGIC much much earlier before applying it to the example. You've referred to "next memory address" a few times in this section, but it's confusing because the concept hasn't been explained yet.
  
  • Instead of stating "starts from address x", could you please add a column "Address" to the three tables, and update "x+1", "x+2" and "x+3" to actual values?
  
  • It'll also help if you add a few examples below the first example, something like: mem[0] = 5, mem[2] = 5, mem[5] = 10. I had spent quite some time before I finally understood what you were trying to say there.

* subleq
  • mem[A] = mem[A] - mem[B]: do you mean the content of the memory at address A is changed?

  • Please change "a label" to "labels".

* @label
  • Please delete the first point as I find it confusing and it seems to just repeat the syntax already shown.

* Execution
  • Please change "A,B" to "A, B".
  
  • Please delete "=" in "value=mem[A]-mem[B]".
  
  • I don't understand why "During execution… plus 3)." is mentioned here. It seems to be explaining subleq again…?

* Table in the last example
  • Suggest to add a heading (e.g. <<Comprehensive example>>) above "The following example".
  
  • Please delete "combines all the directives and".

  • Please fix the typo: ouputs => outputs.

  • Please limit each line in the "explanation" column to 42 characters at most; a line gets cut off when it is too long.
  
Input
* Please format "@IN" as a {{constant}}.

* Please delete "(positive and negatives)".

Output
* Please format "@OUT" as a {{constant}}.

(character limit reached, to be continued…)

(continued)

Constraints
* Suggest to mention that the OISC Assembly program in each case is always valid and does not result in any errors during execution, and delete "For simplicity, it is not necessary to handle errors in the source code." in Goal section.

* Is it correct that in all cases, addresses to jump to are always well-defined? If so, suggest to mention it as a constraint.  (e.g. if the first instruction is subleq, there won't be any subleqs where parameter C = 1.)

* Is it correct that in all cases, subtraction will never result in a number less than -255? If so, suggest to mention it as a constraint.

Cases
* Which cases cover case-insensitivity of (a) instructions and (b) labels?

* I'll further review the cases after the questions I asked above (and possibly more to come) are clarified.

Thanks.

Suggest to revise the first three examples to something like this, so that the explanation is clearer:

https://pastebin.com/uMG7z0yj
(link expires after a month)

Thanks.

In the link above, it seems more accurate to show the last instruction like this instead:

.data -5  | 11      |  251   |  e

and mem[11] = 251 instead of mem[11] = -5.
Thank you, I have started the revisions and I will let you know when I’m done. Sorry for confusing the formatting of constant vs variables :-(

No worries 😉

I'm not 100% sure about the terminology used in my suggestion, so please feel free to correct it where appropriate.

Hi, I tried to better describe the individual instructions, compilation, and step-by-step execution in the text. I added some tests and I'am working on a simplified series of tests to include at the beginning.

Things are somewhat clearer to me now, thanks! And sorry for the extra work..

* Goal

Please add an extra line before <<Assembler Instructions>>>. Also I would remove the right chevron to be more consistent with the section <<Execution>> (I believe it is accidental in the first place).

Please change "[[subleq]] {{A}} {{B}} [{{C}}]" to "[[subleq]] {{A}},{{B}}[,{{C}}]".

Please change "The parameter {{C}} it's optional" to "The parameter {{C}} is optional".

Can you please explain why subleq 5,9 is represented by 05 | 08 in memory ? Should it not be 09 or did I misunderstand ?

Please change "@data+1 points to the address that contains the -15." to "@datazone+1 points to the address that contains -15." in the Execution section.

To clarify something in the Execution example: we output 242 for subleq @out,@pos because we take the address of @datazone == 12 (== 3 * 4subleq before it), add 2 to it and subtract it from @out == 0 ? If so, that one line needs a bit more explanation than "242: (=> two's complement of -14)".

* Constraints
If you don't add very long test cases, it can be reduced to 1 <= [[N]] <= 50.

I love the puzzle, cheers.
I fix the description and added some tests. Let me know what you think. Thanks for your comments!
That's what I am talking about, that "Assembler" "out" "explanation" table with the previous lines explaining the labels in the example are prefect!

Please change "The following example combine" to "The following example combines" and "The result is >0 so it proceed to the next instruction." to "The result is >0 so it proceeds to the next instruction."
